mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 4.5% in a 3-month window, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% in 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a strengthening labor market and consumer spending, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining UNRATE and rising RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime defined by robust consumer spending (RSAFS > 400,000) and strong housing activity (HOUST > 850,000), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns due to overvaluation and increased risk of a market correction within the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS > 400000 and HOUST > 850, or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 for two consecutive months signals weakening economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as corporate earnings growth slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 850,000 units signals strong consumer confidence and economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings benefit from a robust economy.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 850, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates a tight labor market that may lead to wage inflation and central bank tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 for three consecutive months indicates a deepening economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0 for 3 months, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.
